verdict_summary: Confirmed. The zeroize arm of the register block in src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:190-196 omits digest_valid_reg, which its own reset arm clears five lines above at :185. Because :111-112 derive both the tag output and tag_valid from that single register, a security zeroize returns the FSM to idle while leaving the block asserting that it holds a valid tag. Simulation of one unmodified hmac_core shows tag_valid still 1 six cycles after a completed zeroize and still 1 after 200 further idle cycles, so the refresh the arm's own comment promises never occurs. The parent's own tag-capture expression at src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:163 re-asserts as a direct consequence, because the same zeroize strobe clears the parent's tag_valid_reg while the core keeps its flag set, so the parent captures an all-zero tag as if it were a completed result.

evidence.key_observation: On one real hmac_core driven only through its ports, a completed operation reports tag_valid=1 with tag[63:0]=6c2c68f7fb784420. After a completed zeroize the block reports tag_valid=1 ready=1 tag[63:0]=0000000000000000, and 200 idle cycles later tag_valid is still 1, contradicting the comment at src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:192-193 which states the normal update path refreshes the register on a later cycle. The parent's capture-enable expression, recomputed in the harness from src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:163 rather than asserted, re-asserts once after the zeroize. Final tally checks=6 fails=3 witness_hits=1 with all four covers at 1 and result=PASS; the three failures are exactly the three post-zeroize properties, while control_reset_clears_tag_valid, control_normal_run_sets_tag_valid and containment_reset_still_clears pass, so a real reset still clears the flag and the defect is confined to the zeroize arm.
evidence.structural_audit: 35 of 35 gates pass in proof/logs/run.log with result=PASS. The census of the one always_ff at src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:181-209 is reset_arm_assignments=3 against zeroize_arm_assignments=2, computed without naming which registers appear so that a missed match would fail loudly. The gate asserting that no code line in the zeroize arm clears digest_valid_reg strips comment lines first, because the register is named in that arm only inside the comment that justifies leaving it alone: that distinction is the finding. The FSM path the comment depends on is measured at ctrl_idle_write_enable_assertions=1 (raised only in the next_cmd branch at :347) and default_arm_write_enable_clears=1 (:404), with the always_comb default at :329, so an idle engine never performs the promised refresh.
evidence.tree_wide_idiom: The same zeroize strobe is fanned out to two child masked cores at src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:120 and :139. In src/sha512_masked/rtl/sha512_masked_core.sv the zeroize arm mirrors the reset arm register for register, 22 assignments against 22, and it does clear its own digest_valid_reg at :316 exactly as its reset arm does at :290. The parent src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv does the same, 7 assignments against 7, clearing tag_valid_reg in both arms at :204 and :214. The audited module is the only one of the three that treats its validity flag as exempt.
evidence.negative_control: Adding the single omitted assignment to a scratch copy of the file flips the identical testbench: witness_hits=0, tb_fails=0, cov_tag_valid_survives_zeroize=0 and cov_spurious_parent_capture_edge=0 for anti-vacuity, the three violating checks now pass, and both harness controls plus the containment case still pass. The patch is measured at scratch_code_lines_added=1, so no other behaviour was altered. NEGATIVE CONTROL: PASS.
evidence.software_reachability: The zeroize strobe originates in software. src/integration/rtl/caliptra_reg/caliptra_reg.h:962 places the block at 0x10010000, :979 places HMAC512_CTRL at 0x10010010 with the ZEROIZE field at bit 2 (:986-987), :995 places HMAC512_STATUS at 0x10010018 with the VALID bit at bit 1 (:1000-1001), and :1195 places HMAC512_TAG_0 at 0x10010100. src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:259 shows the register field driving zeroize_reg, and :171 shows it reaching the audited core.

security_impact: A zeroize is the operation software uses to make a cryptographic block safe to hand on, and the block's answer to whether it holds a valid result becomes untruthful across exactly that operation. Two consequences follow. Software polling HMAC512_STATUS.VALID after a zeroize reads a set valid bit and may treat the all-zero TAG register as a completed authentication tag, which turns a cleared block into a source of a fixed, attacker-predictable tag value. Independently, the parent's rising-edge capture at src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:163 fires because the zeroize cleared the parent's own copy of the flag while the core kept its flag set, so the parent writes an all-zero tag into the software-readable TAG register at :227 as though a real operation had just completed, and does so after the TAG.hwclr at :267 has already cleared it. Both effects break integrity of the block's results rather than disclosing secrets.
non_findings: No digest material is disclosed. Measurement shows tag[63:0]=0000000000000000 after the zeroize, because the child masked cores clear their own H2_digest on the same strobe (src/sha512_masked/rtl/sha512_masked_core.sv:316). The initial hypothesis that residual digest bits would remain was tested and is wrong, which is why confidentiality is scored none.
Zeroize is not broken in general. The FSM is returned to CTRL_IDLE correctly by the same arm, and the containment case confirms a real reset still clears the flag.

The reported description of this bug as an HMAC LFSR seed width reduction from 384 to 192 bits does not hold in this tree. The seed path is 384 bits consistently at src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:81, src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:39, src/hmac/rtl/hmac_reg.rdl:166-168 (twelve 32-bit HMAC512_LFSR_SEED registers), src/hmac_drbg/rtl/hmac_drbg.sv:55 and src/ecc/rtl/ecc_hmac_drbg_interface.sv:48, matching the 384-bit figure stated in docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:1199. No width inconsistency exists, so no such claim is made. The defect reported here was located independently in the same file and is proved on its own evidence.
The masking-entropy reseed chain in this file is a separate matter and is not relied on by any gate or check here.
proof_integrity: One real hmac_core is instantiated and driven only through its declared ports. The harness contains no force, no deposit and no hierarchical assignment.

The parent consequence is not asserted. The harness recomputes the parent's capture-enable expression from src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:163 and models the parent's tag_valid_reg exactly as src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:196-231 writes it, so the reported edge follows from the parent's own formula applied to the real core output.

The tracking window for that edge opens only after the modelled parent register has settled to 1, verified in the log by the line reading tracking opens with tag_valid=1 parent_tag_valid_reg=1, so the legitimate completion edge cannot be miscounted as the spurious one.
Every structural census is computed from assignment counts independent of which registers are named, so a regex that failed to match would report a wrong count rather than silently pass.
The audited RTL was not modified. The negative control patches a scratch copy only, and the patch size is gated at one added line and zero removed lines.
residual_uncertainty: The proof is at block boundary. It establishes the stale flag, the absent refresh, and the parent's capture edge from the parent's own expression, but it does not run the full integration to enumerate which firmware sequences read the resulting TAG register. The register addresses that make the strobe and the status bit reachable from software are cited from the generated header rather than exercised end to end.

reproduction.how_to_run: bash final_bug_submissions/015/proof/scripts/run_bug_015_proof.sh for the structural audit over the submitted sources; then bash final_bug_submissions/015/proof/scripts/run_bug_015_sim.sh with CALIPTRA_ROOT set to the repository root and VCS on PATH for the directed simulation; then bash final_bug_submissions/015/proof/scripts/run_bug_015_negative_control.sh for the patched-copy control. The audit needs no simulator.
reproduction.expected_result: The audit reports 35 of 35 gates with result=PASS. The simulation reports checks=6 fails=3 witness_hits=1 with cov_reset_clears_tag_valid, cov_tag_valid_after_normal_run, cov_tag_valid_survives_zeroize and cov_spurious_parent_capture_edge all at 1, and result=PASS; the three failing checks are the post-zeroize properties by design. The negative control reports witness_hits=0, tb_fails=0, both defect covers at 0, scratch_code_lines_added=1, and NEGATIVE CONTROL: PASS.
